post_title: Origin Festival 2026: A Psytrance Cycle Odyssey
post_content:
# Origin Festival 2026: A Psytrance Cycle Odyssey

For me, the pilgrimage to a psytrance festival is as important as the event itself. This year, for my birthday, I decided to cycle 300km from my home in Woodstock, Cape Town, to Origin Festival and back.

It wasn't just a ride; it was a meditation. A way to cleanse the mind before entering the psychedelic playground.

![Beautiful sunset over Elgin](figma:asset/dfc0e7ceee6b7f81fd3e6ccf4d7036097bc79477.png)

I watched a beautiful sunset over Elgin, feeling the anticipation building. The energy of the coming gathering was palpable even from kilometers away.

## The Journey Begins

Today's ride to Grabouw via Sir Lowry's pass was 80km of pure adrenaline. I crushed that pass and felt on top of the world. Tomorrow, I celebrate my birthday in style, cycling the final 75km to Origin Festival in Helderstroom. Can't wait for a weekend of stomping, UV vibes, and reuniting with my trance family.

![Conquering Houwhoek Pass](figma:asset/06d4edfbf4b3d5e14311a5a52ea6756b57d2c956.png)

## Festival Magic

I arrived at the party around 11:30 AM on Friday morning, buzzing with endorphins. I skipped the queue, shouted that it was my birthday, and the welcome was overwhelming!

Origin Festival is a staple of the Cape Town psytrance calendar. Thanks to Monique and Reagan for curating such an incredible space—the psychedelic decor, the thumping basslines, and the beautiful souls on the dancefloor were perfection.

I spent the weekend doing what I love most: painting faces in the shade during the day and watching them glow under the UV cannons at night. To my friends, thanks for making me feel so loved. It was a truly magnificent experience.

## The Return Journey

I cycled back to the farm in Elgin on Monday to decompress, and then finally all the way back to Cape Town on Tuesday.

Just conquered the road back to Cape Town after an unforgettable birthday ride. Completed just short of 300km with a 40kg bike pack, 3200m climbing, 14hrs of pure adrenaline and top speed of over 75km/hr.

Time to dive back into work focus and training for the next adventure. The beat goes on! One love & peace out 💚❤️🌈

post_content:
Capturing the vibrant energy and creative spirit of Nation of Gondwana Festival with UV reactive rainbow face paint and body art.

## Nation of Gondwana — Where the Dancefloor Becomes a Canvas

Nation of Gondwana is one of those festivals that *defies description*. Nestled in the forests outside Berlin, it's a three-day celebration of music, art, and community that draws some of the most creative people in Europe.

### The Setup

I set up a small **UV face paint station** near the main stage, armed with neon palettes, a blacklight mirror, and about a hundred hand-cut holographic stickers. The queue started forming before sunset and didn't stop until 4am.

> There's something magical about painting someone's face and watching them transform — not just visually, but in how they carry themselves. Confidence is the best accessory.

### Techniques Used

The rainbow streak designs are built on a simple but effective layering technique:

- **White base layer** for maximum pigment pop under UV
- **Wet-on-wet blending** for seamless rainbow gradients
- **Dot accents** using the back end of a brush for precision
- **Setting spray** to survive hours of dancing

### The Result

Every face became a unique piece of art. No two designs were the same — each one was a collaboration between my vision and the person sitting in front of me. That's what makes festival makeup special: it's *alive*.

post_content:
It was my birthday weekend, I cycled to the event over two days and then cycled home, I brought all my clothes, hammock gear and makeup bags in panniers on my gravel bike. I danced, celebrated and spread the joy of my makeup. I also had some stickers made.

## The Birthday Cycle — 300km to Origin Festival

This one was special. For my birthday, I decided to **cycle from Berlin to Origin Festival** — a two-day ride through the countryside with everything I needed strapped to my gravel bike.

### The Journey

Panniers loaded with:

- Full UV makeup kit (paints, brushes, sponges)
- Hammock and sleeping gear
- Three days of clothes
- A box of *holographic stickers* I had printed for the occasion

> The best adventures start with a stupid idea and a full water bottle.

### At the Festival

Once I arrived, I set up camp in the trees and started painting faces. Birthday energy is *contagious* — people were coming up asking for neon grids, geometric patterns, and third-eye designs all weekend.

### The Stickers

I had a batch of **custom holographic stickers** made for Origin — psychedelic mandalas and UV-reactive designs. Gave them all away. If you got one, you're part of the crew now.

### The Ride Home

Two days of cycling after three days of dancing. My legs were destroyed but my heart was full. Already planning next year's route.
